findings.title: Partial refund now disburses the full order total
findings.evidence: The function signature accepts amount_cents and the preceding comment states it is the partial amount the support agent approved, but the call was changed to pass order.total_cents: '    return gateway.refund(order.txn_id, order.total_cents)'. Reachable path: any support agent calling refund(order, amount_cents) with amount_cents < order.total_cents now issues a gateway refund for the full total, overpaying by (total_cents - amount_cents).
findings.recommendation: Revert to passing the approved partial amount: 'return gateway.refund(order.txn_id, amount_cents)'. If the intent was a full refund path, add a separate explicit function or a validated full_refund(order) that does not silently change partial-refund semantics.

findings.title: amount_cents parameter left unused; no guard against untested refund path
findings.evidence: With '    return gateway.refund(order.txn_id, order.total_cents)' the amount_cents parameter is now dead, so callers keep compiling and passing an approved amount that has no effect, and no bounds/validation test covers the refund amount (no test commands were run). This masks the regression at both call sites and in review.
findings.recommendation: Restore use of amount_cents and add a unit test asserting gateway.refund is called with exactly the approved partial amount (e.g. spy on gateway.refund and assert amount_cents < order.total_cents is forwarded verbatim), plus a validation test rejecting amount_cents <= 0 or amount_cents > order.total_cents.
